security_audit.summary: All static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline Rust identifiers, repository metadata, and a cryptography example. The skill provides standard Rust development guidance and does not show prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples may trigger static command detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that cargo commands are developer validation steps and should run only in trusted project checkouts.

remediation.issue: The signing example lacks context about key handling boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: State that example keys are generated in memory and are not loaded from files or transmitted.

content.value_statement: Rust teams often need consistent guidance for async services, error handling, testing, and package metadata. This skill gives focused patterns for Guts and commonware-based Rust work.
actual_capabilities: Recommends cargo formatting and clippy checks before commit.
Shows boundaries for thiserror in libraries and anyhow in applications.
Outlines public module exports for Rust library structure.
Lists commonware crates for cryptography, p2p, consensus, storage, and codec.
Provides Cargo metadata and lint settings for a Guts crate.
limitations: Does not install Rust toolchains or dependencies by itself.
Focuses on Guts and commonware conventions, not every Rust framework.
Examples are illustrative and may need project-specific types.
Does not replace security review for cryptography or networking changes.

use_cases.title: Align a New Rust Service
use_cases.description: Use the skill to structure modules, errors, async commands, and tests before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Review Guts Project Changes
use_cases.description: Apply consistent checks for documentation, lint settings, Cargo metadata, and commonware crate usage.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Review
use_cases.description: Prompt Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to review Rust work against project-specific conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Rust Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Rust changes for formatting, clippy warnings, and documentation gaps using this skill. Explain the next steps in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design error handling for a Rust library module. Use thiserror for public errors and explain when anyhow should be avoided.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor an Async Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Tokio service design and suggest a channel-based structure with clear request, reply, and shutdown behavior. Include testing considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Commonware Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate a Guts module that uses commonware cryptography, p2p, storage, and codec crates. Identify API boundaries, threat assumptions, and performance checks.

output_examples.input: Review my new Rust service module for this project.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering module exports, async command flow, error boundaries, documentation gaps, and required formatting or lint checks.

output_examples.input: I need a Cargo metadata checklist for a Guts crate.
output_examples.output: A checklist for package fields, Rust edition, license, repository metadata, dependency placement, and lint settings.

output_examples.input: Help plan commonware cryptography use in a feature.
output_examples.output: A design review that separates signing responsibilities, API boundaries, test needs, and security review questions.

best_practices: Run formatting, linting, and tests before asking for final review.
Provide module purpose, error boundaries, and async runtime assumptions.
Ask for security notes when changes touch networking, storage, or cryptography.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad rewrites without naming the Rust module and goal.
Do not treat example types as drop-in APIs without checking the project.
Do not skip tests when changing async command flow or consensus behavior.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for Rust work in the Guts project and similar commonware-based decentralized infrastructure projects.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes cargo commands and Rust patterns. The host assistant decides whether to run tools with user context.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace a Rust security review?
faq.answer: No. Use it for development guidance, then perform dedicated review for cryptography, networking, and storage changes.

faq.question: Does it cover async Rust?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Tokio patterns, channel-based services, and async test structure.

faq.question: Does it require commonware?
faq.answer: The guidance is tailored to commonware, but many Rust style and testing recommendations are still general.
